text:
jamie: FYI reproducible window during a drain where prefill committed a residency record while the lease was still active on the original node. client saw a tombstone then later a resident entry -> bad.
lina: can we get the condensed repro please?
jamie: short trace below:
```
1) read hits nodeA (lease held)
2) eviction kicks, nodeB attempts prefill
3) nodeA locally flips prefix->DEMOTED (read visibility) but lease not yet released
4) nodeB writes residency metadata based on demote view
5) client retry hits nodeA serving tombstone, inconsistent with nodeB
```
oscar: so demote visibility and lease transfer are decoupled. we need a contract preventing prefill from publishing residency unless ownership is confirmed.
anya: options we've considered in past threads but want to pick a pragmatic path: (A) make lease release the single atomic event (big refactor), (B) epoch-guarded prefill commit (CAS on lease_epoch), (C) token/quiesce handshake, (D) two-phase candidate+finalize pattern.
jamie: quick tradeoffs:
- (A) simplest semantics but huge cross-cut change and will lengthen drain operations
- (B) smallest local change; aborts on mismatch, needs cleanup and backoff, may increase retries
- (C) reduces aborts and gives explicit coordination; requires token lifecycle and plumbing across services
- (D) finalizer-based approach provides similar safety to token but keeps ops local to storage via candidate keys; needs GC/TTL and idempotent finalizers
lina: for short-term shipability (and minimal infra churn) I prefer (B) with good backoff and metrics. if abort rate high, we can layer (D) or (C) later.
oscar: agreed. implementation sketch for (B): on prefill start read lease_epoch=E from prefix.meta; prepare residency payload but commit only if prefix.residency_epoch CASes from E to E (or write a generation-tagged resident bit using backend CAS semantics). if CAS fails abort and fallback to read-through. ensure writes are atomic to avoid partial resident blobs.
jamie: details to watch:
- multi-writer races: multiple nodes may observe same E and race; first CAS wins, others abort and fallback
- aborted partial writes: use the storage generation tag or a transient candidate key to avoid visible partial state
- retry/backoff: exponential backoff with jitter, metric prefill_retries, and a give-up threshold where we stop trying and let the client read-through
- metric surface: prefill_cas_failures, prefill_attempts, prefill_backoff_seconds, prefill_success_per_attempt
anya: a small finalizer can be added in the same rollout: when CAS fails and candidate key exists remove it (GC). mark candidate keys TTL=30s to bound GC work. finalizer is idempotent.
oscar: testing plan: unit tests for CAS success/fail paths; micro-sim that injects demote-vs-lease inconsistencies and asserts no stale residency visible; chaos canary: run drain storms with prefill-heavy workload and watch prefill_cas_failures and user-visible error rate.
lina: roll plan: feature-flag the epoch-guard commit, ship small patch behind flag, run canary for 48h, if CAS abort rate > X% or prefill retries increase tail latency significantly, escalate to token/quiesce prototype.
jamie: operational note: we must avoid thundering herd on aborted prefills. implement a randomized backoff with capped max attempts; after N failed attempts record a throttled fallback and let client read-through instead of spinning.
anya: also consider an optimization: prefer local read-through if prefix had recent demote event within threshold T; avoids wasting time prefetching during active ownership change. metric: prefetch_suppressed_due_to_recent_demote.
oscar: good call. that heuristic reduces wasted writes and is low-risk.
orchestrator-bot: canary scheduled: drain-storm-run-2025-04-02 -> tagging owners @jamie @lina (please attach PR when ready).
jamie: I'll implement the CAS commit using generation-tag write and a candidate key TTL fallback. target branch: prefill/epoch-cas-guard-1779. expect draft PR today, tests tomorrow.
lina: I'll own the unit/integration tests and the canary harness. will add metrics dashboards for prefill_cas_failures and prefetch_suppressed_due_to_recent_demote.
anya: follow-up action items summary:
- jamie: PR implementing epoch-guarded CAS + candidate key TTL + feature flag
- lina: tests, canary config, dashboards
- oscar: run chaos sim and review metric thresholds for escalation
- team: if abort rate high -> prototype token/quiesce (separate RFC)
jamie: leaving thread open for follow-ups and will post the PR link when ready. thanks.
